section.title: Introduction to Subprograms
section.content: Subprograms (or sub-algorithms) are independent blocks of instructions, identified by a name, that can be called from anywhere in an algorithm. They form the cornerstone of modularity: they allow decomposing a complex problem into simpler, reusable, and easy-to-maintain sub-problems.

bulletPoints.point: ✅ Avoid code duplication: the same sequence of instructions can be used multiple times without being rewritten.
✅ Improve readability: a well-structured algorithm becomes clearer and easier to understand.
✅ Facilitate maintenance: fixing a bug in a subprogram fixes all its calls.
💻 Two main types: functions (which return a value) and procedures (which return nothing).
💻 Example: use calculateAverage() instead of repeating the calculation.

section.title: Functions
section.content: A function is a subprogram that returns a value.

bulletPoints.point: 💻 Syntax: Function functionName(parameters) : Type Return value EndFunction.
💻 Example: Function sum(a, b : Integer) : Integer Return a + b EndFunction.
💻 Call: result ← sum(3, 4)
▶️ Can have zero parameters.
▶️ Example power: Function power(base : Real, exp : Integer) : Real result ← 1 For i from 1 to exp do result ← result * base EndFor Return result EndFunction.

section.title: Procedures
section.content: A procedure performs actions without returning a value.

bulletPoints.point: 💻 Syntax: Procedure procedureName(parameters) EndProcedure.
💻 Example: Procedure displayWelcome(name) Display("Hello ", name) EndProcedure.
▶️ Example swap: Procedure swap(a, b by Reference) temp ← a a ← b b ← temp EndProcedure.
▶️ Procedures often modify the state of the program.

section.title: Parameters: Value vs Reference
section.content: Parameters can be passed by value or by reference.

bulletPoints.point: ▶️ By value: Procedure increment(v) v ← v + 1 EndProcedure. → does not change the original variable
▶️ By reference: Procedure incrementRef(v by Reference) v ← v + 1 EndProcedure. → modifies the original variable
▶️ Choose according to need (read vs modification).

section.title: Local and Global Variables
section.content: The scope of a variable defines where it is accessible.

bulletPoints.point: ▶️ Local variables: visible only within the subprogram.
▶️ Global variables: visible everywhere.
▶️ Prefer parameters rather than globals.
💻 Example: Variables x, y Function sum() Return x + y EndFunction.
▶️ A local variable masks a global one with the same name.
✔️ Must have a base case.
▶️ Factorial: Function fact(n) If n = 0 Then Return 1 Else Return n * fact(n-1) EndFunction.
▶️ Fibonacci: Function fib(n) If n = 0 Then Return 0 If n = 1 Then Return 1 Else Return fib(n-1) + fib(n-2) EndFunction.
⚠️ Be careful of stack overflow.

💻 Grade management: Procedure readGrades(tab, n) Read(n) For i from 1 to n do Read(tab[i]) EndFor EndProcedure
Function average(tab, n) sum ← 0 For i from 1 to n do sum ← sum + tab[i] EndFor Return sum / n EndFunction
💻 Recursive power: Function powerRec(base, exp) If exp = 0 Then Return 1 Else Return base * powerRec(base, exp-1) EndFunction.
✔️ Explicit names.
✔️ Single responsibility.
✔️ Limit parameters.
▶️ Use value / reference correctly.
✔️ Always define a base case in recursion.
✔️ Avoid side effects.
